bullets.text: Ambit expects LME to fall to $2,800/t; at $2,600/t FY28 EPS is Rs36 for VAML and Rs86 for Hindalco, both SELL.
bullets.source: Ambit — Metals & Mining: Non-ferrous - when 'priced in' isn't priced in

detail.summary: Ambit argues metal stocks price the next leg down, not spot, so investors treating VAML/Hindalco as floored at $2,800/t LME are exposed. A fall to that level would force analysts to reset models lower and trigger another round of earnings cuts.
points: Hindalco ~10x, VAML ~9x FY28E EPS at that price
Models would reset to $2,500-2,600/t after the fall
LME -10% means high-beta upstream stocks fall more

bullets.text: Ambit sees greatest risk in non-ferrous at current levels, prefers ferrous; SELL order ends Hindalco > Vedanta, as lower LME weighs on Hindalco India and VAML.
bullets.source: Ambit — Ambit Metals: 2QFY27 Preview- Steel resilient, aluminium vulnerable

detail.summary: Ambit's 2QFY27 preview favours steel over non-ferrous, flagging lower LME prices as the drag on Hindalco India and VAML. Steelmakers still face QoQ EBITDA declines from mix and lagged contract pricing.
points: Rs700-1,900/t QoQ EBITDA decline: Tata Steel, JSW Steel, Jindal Steel
SELL pecking order: JSW > Tata > Jindal > NMDC > Hindalco > Vedanta

bullets.text: Ambit sees Rs700-1,900/t QoQ EBITDA decline for Tata, JSW, Jindal Steel; SELL order JSW > Tata > Jindal > NMDC; BUY JSL > Shyam.
bullets.source: Ambit — Ambit Metals: 2QFY27 Preview- Steel resilient, aluminium vulnerable

detail.summary: NSRs should contract QoQ on product mix and lagged contracted pricing, even though HRC rose while rebar fell. Ambit sees greatest risk in non-ferrous at current levels and prefers ferrous over non-ferrous.
points: EBITDA/t down Rs700-1,900 for Tata, JSW, Jindal Steel
Tata Steel UK subdued on shutdown costs; TSN margins improve
SELL: JSW > Tata > Jindal > NMDC > Hindalco > Vedanta

bullets.text: Elara expects flat steel to beat long in 2QFY27, EBITDA/t falling Rs40-1,870; Tata Steel top pick; NMDC EBITDA/t seen -9% QoQ.
bullets.source: Elara — Metals & Mining - Flat steel to outperform long steel - Quarterly Preview

detail.summary: Firm HRC limited seasonal pressure on flat producers, while primary rebar and semis corrected and coking coal is a headwind. Tata Steel's decline is smallest on better European profitability.
points: Jindal Stainless consolidated EBITDA +8% QoQ on volumes

bullets.text: Morgan Stanley: JSW Steel 2QFY27 India crude output 7.07mnt, +11% QoQ; sees ~15% YoY domestic sales growth; Overweight, PT Rs1,470.
bullets.source: Morgan Stanley — PULSE: JSW Steel Ltd.: F2Q27 Production Volume Update

detail.summary: Vijaynagar BF3 ramp-up lifted production sequentially, and with demand good, strong output plus inventory destocking likely drove strong sales growth. Morgan Stanley's sales estimate is adjusted for the BPSL slump sale.
points: India crude steel 7.07mnt, ~5% YoY ex-BPSL base
JSW USA Ohio 0.20mnt vs 0.24mnt year ago

bullets.text: Nomura: Oct hikes of ~Rs10/bag are a start, but petcoke at $184/t (+25% q-q) needs Rs12-15/bag; UltraTech and Dalmia top picks.
bullets.source: Nomura — India cement - Fuel cost inflation raises the pricing hurdle

detail.summary: Fuel inflation has intensified after 2QFY27, so the industry needs more than the announced hikes. Most cost pressure lands in 4QFY27 given 60-90 day lag, so October absorption before the festive slowdown decides 3QFY27 margins.
points: Monitor Oct realisation and pace of further hikes

bullets.text: IIFL cuts FY27-29 cement EBITDA 6-7% and target multiples 10%; 2Q industry EBITDA/t seen Rs833 (-20% q-q); UltraTech, JK Cement preferred.
bullets.source: IIFL — Cement - 2QFY27 preview - Weak quarter, but attractive valuations - UTCEM and JKCE Preferred Picks

detail.summary: Volumes were healthy but the industry could not pass on costs, so realisations were flat while costs rose. Sector has derated 20% in 12 months and trades below long-term averages, which IIFL says largely prices in the weak quarter.
points: Ambuja and JK Lakshmi preferred on valuation

bullets.text: Elara sees 2Q cement EBITDA/t at ~Rs825, lowest since early CY25, EBITDA -26% q-q; petcoke +19% in a month; Shree top pick. (+1 more in Outlook)
bullets.source: Elara — Cement - Margin to hit 1.5-year low - Quarterly Preview (+1 more in Outlook)

detail.summary: Elevated fuel prices and negative operating leverage outweigh healthy volumes, keeping variable costs inflationary into 3QFY27. Shree is preferred for its green-power insulation and North exposure, while Dalmia faces the sharpest decline on weak East pricing.
points: Dalmia sharpest EBITDA/t decline; East prices weak

bullets.text: Elara expects NMDC 2QFY27 EBITDA/t down ~9% QoQ on 2% lower realisations and ~5% seasonal volume decline.
bullets.source: Elara — Metals & Mining - Flat steel to outperform long steel - Quarterly Preview

detail.summary: Elara's Q2 preview favours flat steel over long steel, with Tata Steel its top pick. NMDC is the weak spot in mining: seasonally lower volumes and softer iron ore prices compress per-tonne margins despite higher YoY volumes.
points: Sales volumes down ~5% QoQ, up ~4% YoY
Top sector pick remains Tata Steel

bullets.text: CLSA: Sep-26 power demand +11% YoY, merchant prices 2x; prefers regulated NTPC, NHPC, CESC over merchant and coal plays.
bullets.source: CLSA — India power pulse - Strong 2QFY27

detail.summary: CLSA calls 2QFY27 strong for both regulated and merchant power players, but argues the energy crisis and structural turn favour cheaper regulated utilities over expensive merchant power, JSWE, coal plays and TPWR.
points: Base demand +11% YoY, peak +17% YoY in Sep-26
Merchant prices 2x; Rs20/kWh peak on 14 days

bullets.text: Nuvama keeps Dixon at HOLD with estimates unchanged on the Gemtek optical-transceiver JV; earnings impact seen modest initially.
bullets.source: Nuvama — Nuvama Daily: Actionables: Banking, Sagility & IKS - IC, Dixon, Jubilant food | Zydus Life, Q2FY27 Earnings Preview

detail.summary: Nuvama calls the formally incorporated JV moderately positive because it extends Dixon into telecom and optical connectivity, helped by its ECMS approval. Near-term earnings contribution is small, so the house leaves numbers and its HOLD rating untouched.
points: 60:40 JV with Taiwan's Gemtek, via Dixon Electroconnect
Products: SFPs, BOSA and other telecom items
Binding agreement had been announced earlier

bullets.text: Dixon takes 60% of Dixon Electroconnect, its Gemtek JV for optical transceivers (SFP, BOSA), targeting AI, cloud and data-centre networking demand.
bullets.source: Nomura — India Consumer Durables and EMS: Dixon Technologies signs JV pact with Gemtek to manufacture optical transceivers

detail.summary: Nomura's morning news note relays Dixon's BSE filing on the JV. It pairs Dixon's large-scale manufacturing with Gemtek's high-speed optical module expertise to enter the data-centre, telecom and optical-connectivity ecosystem.
points: 60% Dixon stake in Dixon Electroconnect Pvt Ltd
Makes SFP and BOSA optical transceivers in India
Demand drivers: AI, cloud, hyperscale data centres
Same note: Amazon India sees 35-40% festive demand spike

bullets.text: TCS 2QFY27 cc growth 0.5% QoQ matched Kotak's estimate; EBIT margin 24.0% flat, TCV $9.6bn -4% YoY; Kotak keeps ADD, FV Rs2,320.
bullets.source: Kotak — [Kotak[ TCS (Rs2077, ADD): First take-- inline quarter driven by international business; muted deal wins

detail.summary: Kotak calls the quarter in line, led by international (+1.2% QoQ) while the US grew modestly. Margin held but the note says business challenges appear to outweigh ability to protect profitability. At 13x FY28E EPS, valuation already discounts prolonged low single digit growth.
points: Adj EBIT margin 24.0%, flat QoQ, down 120bps YoY

bullets.text: ICICI Sec keeps TCS REDUCE, TP Rs1,920 (from 1,860): H1FY27 TCV down 1.5% YoY, US and Continental Europe soft, margins ~24% through FY28.
bullets.source: ICICI Securities — Tata Consultancy Services (REDUCE): Moderation in deal TCV continues; core markets of America and Continental Europe remain soft

detail.summary: ICICI expects muted FY27-28 growth: UK drove the quarter while US and Continental Europe stayed soft, and management said demand has not materially changed. Pricing pressure from front-loaded productivity sharing and growth investments cap margins. Valued at 12x FY28E EPS.
points: Cc growth 0.5% QoQ vs ICICI and consensus 0.6%
MHP acquisition ~50bps dilutive to Q4FY27 EBIT margin
Best Buy and $1.45bn Porsche deals excluded from TCV

bullets.text: US DoL suspended new and pending PERM applications for TCS, Infosys, HCLT, Wipro, Cognizant, Capgemini; Kotak sees no meaningful delivery or earnings impact.
bullets.source: Kotak — [Kotak] IT Services: An event of limited impact (+17 more in Outlook)

detail.summary: Kotak says the suspension reinforces an unfavourable immigration direction but has limited operational relevance, as Indian IT has localised US workforces and visa-dependent staff are a small, declining share. Risk turns material only if curbs reach existing work authorisation or client-site deployment.
points: Treatment of pending PERM cases unclear
Higher subcontractor use may pressure near-term costs

bullets.text: UBS: RBI hiked repo 25bp to 5.5% and turned to calibrated tightening; expects 50-75bp cumulative, next 25bp in December, Brent $95 FY27.
bullets.source: UBS — UBS INDIA - BHARTI raises tariffs | Eco after RBI MPC - Expect 50-75bps hike/Liquidity/INR underperformance

detail.summary: Inflation running above 5.5% for three quarters from Q3FY27 is what drives the 50-75bp call. Higher oil, a wider current account deficit and weaker rainfall are expected to soften 2HFY27 growth despite the GDP upgrade.
points: RBI FY27 GDP 7.1%, CPI 5.2%; UBS GDP 7.2%
Brent $100 in Dec quarter, $95 FY27 average

bullets.text: CLSA: S&P above 7,800 with US 10Y at 5.3% flips the Fed model to favour bonds for the first time since 2002; only 5% 12M upside.
bullets.source: CLSA — CLSA: Global equity strategy: Fed model matters

detail.summary: A 135bp rise in the 10Y yield has pushed the earnings yield to bond yield spread negative. Record US equity exposure, extreme Mag7 earnings concentration and slowing liquidity argue for caution, though TIPS near 3% and robust earnings may stabilise the spread.
points: S&P EPS 34% above trend; Mag7 58% of growth

bullets.text: CLSA Macrometer: August growth moderates but tracks above RBI's 7.2% 2QFY27 GDP estimate; M3 17.4%, CPI 4.9% at 20-month high. (+4 more in Outlook)
bullets.source: CLSA — CLSA: India strategy (Macrometer): Still strong (+4 more in Outlook)

detail.summary: High-frequency indicators show August momentum easing mainly in manufacturing and mining, while consumption and liquidity stay strong. Early September data suggest some recovery, with the liquidity-policy trade-off and the Middle East conflict the key risks.
points: 40% of core indicators beat estimate, 34% miss
Manufacturing PMI weaker for third straight month

bullets.text: JPM 2QFY27 auto preview: PV margins likely bottom in 2Q; prefers TVSL, HMCL, Motherson, M&M, Maruti, TMCV; M&M earnings seen +5% YoY.
bullets.source: JPM — India Autos: Commodity inflation continues to deflate investor sentiment, 2W/CV/Ancs should do better than PVs… 2QFY27 preview

detail.summary: Revenue growth is strong on volume recovery, but OEMs chose volume over margin in the commodity upcycle, so EBITDA lags. PVs take the most margin erosion; 2W, CV and ancillaries fare better, and bigger PV price hikes are expected after the festive season.
points: Maruti and Hyundai earnings to fall sharply YoY
TMCV EBITDA growth >20% despite gross margin pressure
Bajaj, TVS offset inflation via exports and INR
Commodity cost index peaked in 2Q; steel, rubber still higher

bullets.text: Avendus 2QFY27 preview: Dixon revenue +25-30% QoQ on mobile price hikes; Kaynes likely weakest print since IPO; steel EBITDA/t falls across the pack ex-SAIL.
bullets.source: Avendus Spark — Call NOW @11am - CV Dealer - AL/MM (South) | OYO DRHP and PAYTM ARA | IC on Aether | Previews 2Q'27 | RBI Rate Hike

detail.summary: Avendus sees EMS revenue strong except Kaynes, with margins the debate. Metals face squeezed unit EBITDA as realisations fall and coking coal costs rise, with aluminium hit by lower LME and higher alumina.
points: Dixon margins pencilled lower on PLI phase-out, room to surprise
Kaynes flattish-to-lower revenue on smart metering slump
Jindal Steel EBITDA/t Rs10.2k vs Rs12k, -15% QoQ
SAIL EBITDA/t ~Rs10.1k, holds on operating leverage

ai_semis.source: GuruFocus.com — AMD Stocks Fall 1.5% Despite TSMC's Record AI Demand Signal (2026-10-08)

ai_semis.source: TheStreet — AMD CEO delivers stark warning on chip market's future (2026-10-09)
